references.text: Matthew's parallel account of the seed that fell among thorns, where the thorns grew up and choked it.
Mark's parallel account of the seed that fell among thorns and was choked, so that it did not bear fruit.
Jesus' own explanation of what the seed among thorns means: those who hear the word, but are choked by life's worries, riches, and pleasures, and do not produce mature fruit.
Matthew's rendering of Jesus' explanation: the one who hears the word, but the cares of this world and the deceitfulness of riches choke the word, so it becomes unfruitful.
Mark's rendering of Jesus' explanation: those who hear the word, but the worries of this life, the deceitfulness of riches, and desires for other things come in and choke the word.
After the fall into sin, God cursed the ground so that it would produce thorns and thistles—a fundamental background for the symbolism of thorns as an obstacle and a curse.
Jeremiah uses the image of sowing among thorns as a warning to Judah and Jerusalem not to let evil prevent God's word from bearing fruit.
Paul warns against the desire for riches that leads people into ruin—parallel to the choking effect of thorns in the parable.
The book of Hebrews uses an agricultural image where land that produces thorns and thistles is worthless and under a curse, paralleling the unfruitful result when thorns choke the seed.
